- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for near-term (1–7d) horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% for short-term (1–7d) to align with bearish momentum.
- After a sharp spike in sentiment (e.g., 1.00), model frequently overreacts with exaggerated overshoot; cap forecast at 1.5x recent high for 3–7d horizon.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods when sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67); add 0.1–0.3 to forecast for 8–30d horizon if sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30d horizon, model often fails to capture long-term sentiment drift; adjust by adding 0.1–0.4 to forecast if sentiment >0.67 over last 7d, or subtract 0.1–0.3 if sentiment <0.33.
- Avoid forecasting below 0.10 in 30d horizon unless sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.10) and recent price is trending down.
